sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第073卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Governance, Volume 73
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 73

sentences.zh: 【魏紀五】起旃蒙單閼，盡強圉大荒落，凡三年。

translations.literal: [Wei Records Five] Beginning with Zhanmeng Danyan, ending with Qiangyu Dahuangluo, three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Wei Records, Five] spans from the year Zhanmeng-Danyan through Qiangyu-Dahuangluo—a period of three years.

sentences.zh: 烈祖明皇帝中之下青龍三年（

translations.literal: Illustrious Ancestor Emperor Ming, middle scroll, lower part, Qinglong year three (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming the Illustrious Ancestor, Part Two (conclusion), Qinglong year 3 (

sentences.zh: 乙卯，公元二三五年）

translations.literal: Yimao, the year 235 of the Common Era)
translations.idiomatic: yimao cycle, AD 235)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊子，以大將軍司馬懿為太尉。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on day Wuzi, Grand General Sima Yi was appointed Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the day wuzi, Grand General Sima Yi was made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，皇太后郭氏殂。

translations.literal: On day Dingsi, Empress Dowager Guo passed away.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingsi, Empress Dowager Guo died.

sentences.zh: 帝數問甄后死狀於太后，由是太后以憂殂。

translations.literal: The Emperor repeatedly questioned the Empress Dowager about the circumstances of Empress Zhen's death; because of this the Empress Dowager died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kept pressing the empress dowager about how Empress Zhen had died, and she died of distress as a result.

sentences.zh: 漢楊儀既殺魏延，自以為有大功，宜代諸葛亮秉政；

translations.literal: In Han, Yang Yi, having killed Wei Yan, considered that he had achieved a great merit and ought to replace Zhuge Liang in holding power;
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Yi of Shu killed Wei Yan, he believed his deed merited great reward and that he should succeed Zhuge Liang as head of government;

sentences.zh: 而亮平生密指，以儀狷狹，意在蔣琬。

translations.literal: but in his lifetime Liang had secretly indicated that Yi was narrow and obstinate, and that his intent lay with Jiang Wan.
translations.idiomatic: but Zhuge Liang had privately indicated that Yi was narrow-minded and obstinate, and that he intended Jiang Wan to take his place.

sentences.zh: 儀至成都，拜中軍師，無所統領，從容而已。

translations.literal: When Yi reached Chengdu, he was appointed Central Army Adviser, with nothing to command—at ease and nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi arrived in Chengdu, he was named Central Army Adviser but given no troops to command—an idle post, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 初，儀事昭烈帝為尚書，琬時為尚書郎。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yi had served the Founding Emperor as Director of the Masters of Writing, while Wan was then a Master of Writing Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yi had served Emperor Zhaolie as Director of the Masters of Writing while Wan was still a junior clerk in that office.

sentences.zh: 後雖俱為丞相參軍、長史，儀每從行，當其勞劇；

translations.literal: Later, although both were staff officers and chief clerks to the Chancellor, Yi always accompanied on campaign and bore the heavy toil;
translations.idiomatic: Later, though both served as staff officer and chief clerk to the chancellor, Yi always marched with the army and shouldered the hardest work;

sentences.zh: 自謂年宦先琬，才能逾之，於是怨憤形於聲色，歎吒之音發於五內，時人畏其言語不節，莫敢從也。

translations.literal: he considered that in years and office he preceded Wan and that his talent surpassed his, and thus resentment and anger showed in his voice and countenance, sounds of lament and outcry issuing from within; people of the time feared his lack of restraint in speech and none dared follow him.
translations.idiomatic: He thought himself senior to Wan in age and rank and more capable besides, and his resentment showed plainly in voice and face—groans and outbursts from the depths of his being. Men of the day feared his intemperate tongue and kept their distance.

sentences.zh: 惟後軍師費禕往慰省之，儀對禕恨望，前後云云。

translations.literal: Only Rear Army Adviser Fei Yi went to console and visit him; Yi answered Yi with resentment and longing, back and forth at length.
translations.idiomatic: Only Rear Army Adviser Fei Yi went to comfort him; Yang Yi poured out his grievances to Fei Yi at great length.

sentences.zh: 又語禕曰：「往者丞相亡沒之際，吾若舉軍以就魏氏，處世寧當落度如此邪！

translations.literal: He also said to Yi: "In the past, at the time when the Chancellor died, if I had led the army to submit to Wei, would I in this world have fallen to such a low state!
translations.idiomatic: He also told Fei Yi, "When the chancellor died, if I had led the army over to Wei, would I be living in such degradation now!

sentences.zh: 令人追悔，不可復及！

translations.literal: It makes one look back in regret—nothing can be recovered!
translations.idiomatic: The thought fills one with regret—and it can never be undone!

sentences.zh: 」禕密表其言。

translations.literal: " Yi secretly memorialized his words.
translations.idiomatic: " Fei Yi reported his words to the throne in a secret memorial.

sentences.zh: 漢主廢儀為民，徙漢嘉郡。

translations.literal: The Han ruler degraded Yi to commoner status and exiled him to Hanjia commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Shu stripped Yi of rank and banished him to Hanjia commandery as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 儀至徙所，復上書誹謗。

translations.literal: When Yi reached his place of exile, he again submitted a memorial of slander.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi reached his place of exile, he submitted another memorial full of slander.

sentences.zh: ，辭指激切。

translations.literal: Its wording and import were sharp and vehement.
translations.idiomatic: The language was fierce and uncompromising.

sentences.zh: 遂下郡收儀，儀自殺。

translations.literal: Thereupon the commandery was ordered to take Yi into custody; Yi killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery was ordered to arrest him; Yi took his own life.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚寅，葬文德皇后。

translations.literal: Third month, on day Gengyin, Empress Wende was buried.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day gengyin, Empress Wende was interred.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，漢主以蔣琬為大將軍、錄尚書事；

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, the Han ruler appointed Jiang Wan Grand General and Recorder of Affairs for the Masters of Writing;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, the ruler of Shu made Jiang Wan Grand General with authority to oversee the Masters of Writing;

sentences.zh: 費禕代琬為尚書令。

translations.literal: Fei Yi replaced Wan as Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi succeeded Wan as Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 帝好土功，既作許昌宮，又治洛陽宮，起昭陽太極殿，築總章觀，高十餘丈。

translations.literal: The Emperor was fond of earthworks; having already built the Xuchang palace, he also renovated the Luoyang palace, raised the Zhaoyang and Taiji halls, and constructed the Zongzhang Pavilion, more than ten zhang in height.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved grand construction. After finishing the palace at Xuchang, he turned to Luoyang—raising the Zhaoyang and Taiji halls and building the Zongzhang Pavilion to a height of more than ten zhang.

sentences.zh: 力役不已，農桑失業。

translations.literal: Corvée labor did not cease; farming and sericulture were neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Forced labor never let up, and farming and sericulture were abandoned.

sentences.zh: 司空陳群上疏曰：「昔禹承唐、虞之盛，猶卑宮室而惡衣服。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Chen Qun submitted a memorial saying: "In the past Yu inherited the flourishing age of Tang and Yu, yet still kept his palaces lowly and disdained fine clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Chen Qun memorialized the throne: "Even Yu, inheriting the golden age of Tang and Shun, kept his dwellings humble and his dress plain.

sentences.zh: 況今喪亂之後，人民至少，比漢文、景之時，不過一大郡。

translations.literal: How much more so now, after the age of ruin and chaos—the people are very few; compared with the time of Emperors Wen and Jing of Han, it amounts to no more than one large commandery.
translations.idiomatic: How much more so today, after generations of war—the population is tiny; compared with the reigns of Han Wen and Jing, we amount to little more than a single large commandery.

sentences.zh: 加以邊境有事，將士勞苦，若有水旱之患，國家之深憂也。

translations.literal: Moreover, there are troubles on the borders and officers and soldiers suffer toil; if there should be flood or drought, that would be a deep worry for the state.
translations.idiomatic: The frontiers are active and the troops exhausted; flood or drought on top of that would be a grave national crisis.

sentences.zh: 昔劉備自成都至白水，多作傳捨，興費人役，太祖知其疲民也。

translations.literal: In the past Liu Bei, from Chengdu to Baishui, built many relay lodges, raising costs in labor and corvée; the Founding Emperor knew this exhausted the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei built relay stations all the way from Chengdu to Baishui, he wasted labor and exhausted the people—our founding emperor saw through it at once.

sentences.zh: 今中國勞力，亦吳、蜀之所願。

translations.literal: Now if the Central State exhausts its labor, that too is what Wu and Shu would wish.
translations.idiomatic: If we exhaust our own strength now, Wu and Shu will be only too pleased.

sentences.zh: 此安危之機也，惟陛下慮之！

translations.literal: This is the hinge of security and danger—may Your Majesty consider it!
translations.idiomatic: This is the turning point between safety and ruin—may Your Majesty weigh it carefully!

sentences.zh: 」帝答曰：「王業、宮室，亦宜並立。

translations.literal: " The Emperor replied: "Royal enterprise and palaces should also be established together.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor answered, "A royal enterprise and its palaces ought to be raised together.

sentences.zh: 滅賊之後，但當罷守禦耳，豈可復興役邪！

translations.literal: After the rebels are destroyed, one need only end border defense—that is all; how could corvée be raised again!
translations.idiomatic: Once the enemy is destroyed we need only stand down the garrisons—surely we will not keep pressing the people into labor!

sentences.zh: 是固君之職，蕭何之大略也。

translations.literal: This is indeed a ruler's duty—the great strategy of Xiao He.
translations.idiomatic: That is a ruler's proper duty—the grand design of Xiao He himself.

sentences.zh: 」群曰：「昔漢祖惟與項羽爭天下，羽已滅，宮室燒焚，是以蕭何建武庫、太倉，皆是要急，然高祖猶非其壯麗。

translations.literal: " Qun said: "In the past the Founder of Han had only Xiang Yu to contend with for the realm; when Yu was destroyed the palaces were burned, and so Xiao He built the armory and the great granary—all were urgent necessities, yet the High Ancestor still disapproved of their grandeur.
translations.idiomatic: " Chen Qun replied, "When the Han founder fought Xiang Yu for the empire, the palaces were burned to ash after Xiang's fall. Xiao He then built the armory and the great granary—urgent necessities all—yet Gaozu still found them too grand.

sentences.zh: 今二虜未平，誠不宜與古同也。

translations.literal: Now the two barbarian foes are not yet pacified—it truly is not fitting to act as in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Our two enemies are not yet subdued—we truly ought not to take antiquity as our model.

sentences.zh: 夫人之所欲，莫不有辭，況乃天王，莫之敢違。

translations.literal: What people desire, none lacks a reason; how much more the Son of Heaven—none dares disobey.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever people desire, they can always justify—and how much more a Son of Heaven, whom none dare refuse.

sentences.zh: 前欲壞武庫，謂不可不壞也；

translations.literal: Before, when you wished to destroy the armory, it was said it could not but be destroyed;
translations.idiomatic: When you first wished to tear down the armory, it was argued that it had to come down;

sentences.zh: 後欲置之，謂不可不置也。

translations.literal: later when you wished to keep it, it was said it could not but be kept.
translations.idiomatic: when you later wished to keep it, it was argued that it had to stand.

sentences.zh: 若必作之，固非臣下辭言所屈；

translations.literal: If you must build it, it is certainly not within subordinates' words to bend you;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty insists on building, no words of ours can turn you;

sentences.zh: 若少留神，卓然回意，亦非臣下之所及也。

translations.literal: but if you would give a little attention and outstandingly turn your mind, that too is not within what subordinates can achieve.
translations.idiomatic: but if Your Majesty would pause and change course of your own accord, that is beyond what any subject can accomplish for you.

sentences.zh: 漢明帝欲起德陽殿，鐘離意諫，即用其言，後乃復作之；

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Han wished to raise the Deyang Hall; Zhongli Yi remonstrated, and he immediately took his advice, yet later built it again;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Han wished to build the Deyang Hall; Zhongli Yi remonstrated, and the emperor at once accepted his counsel—yet later built it anyway;

sentences.zh: 殿成，謂群臣曰：『鐘離尚書在，不得成此殿也。

translations.literal: when the hall was completed he said to the assembled ministers: "If Director Zhongli were still here, this hall could not have been completed.
translations.idiomatic: when the hall was finished he told his ministers, "If Director Zhongli were still alive, this hall would never have been built.

sentences.zh: 』夫王者豈憚一臣！

translations.literal: " Would a king fear a single minister!
translations.idiomatic: " A king does not fear a single minister!

sentences.zh: 蓋為百姓也。

translations.literal: It was for the sake of the common people.
translations.idiomatic: He did it for the people's sake.

sentences.zh: 今臣曾不能少凝聖德，不及意遠矣。

translations.literal: Now your servant has not been able even slightly to concentrate Your sagely virtue—I fall far short of Yi's intent.
translations.idiomatic: As for me, I have not even slightly checked Your Majesty's resolve—I am no Zhongli Yi.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃為之少有減省。

translations.literal: " The Emperor thereupon somewhat reduced and economized on the project.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then scaled the works back somewhat.

sentences.zh: 帝耽於內寵，婦官秩石擬百官之數，自貴人以下至掖庭灑掃者，凡數千人，選女子知書可付信者六人，以為女尚書，使典省外奏事，處當畫可。

translations.literal: The Emperor was addicted to inner favorites; the ranks and salaries of palace women matched the numbers of the hundred officials—from Honored Lady down to those who swept the Rear Palace, several thousand in all. Six women who could read and were trustworthy were chosen as female Masters of Writing to manage outside memorials to the provinces and decide what should be approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was absorbed in his harem. Palace women's ranks and stipends rivaled those of the civil bureaucracy—from honored ladies down to the sweepers of the rear apartments, they numbered in the thousands. Six literate, trustworthy women were made female Masters of Writing to handle provincial memorials and mark approvals.

sentences.zh: 廷尉高柔上疏曰：「昔漢文惜十家之資，不營小台之娛；

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Gao Rou submitted a memorial saying: "In the past Emperor Wen of Han cherished the resources of ten households and would not build a small terrace for pleasure;
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Gao Rou memorialized: "Emperor Wen of Han would not squander the livelihood of ten households on a pleasure terrace;

sentences.zh: 去病臣匈奴之害，不遑治第之事。

translations.literal: Huo Qubing, having subdued the harm of the Xiongnu, had no leisure for building mansions.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Qubing, once he had crushed the Xiongnu threat, had no time to build himself a mansion.

sentences.zh: 況今所損者非惟百金之費，所憂者非徒北鍬之患乎！

translations.literal: How much more so now—the harm is not only a cost in hundreds of gold; the worry is not merely trouble from northern hoes!
translations.idiomatic: Today the cost is not a mere hundred in gold, and the danger is not a trifling northern frontier alone!

sentences.zh: 可粗成見所營立以充朝宴之儀，訖罷作者，使得就養；

translations.literal: What has already been built may be roughly completed to suffice for court banquets; when construction ends, let the people return to their livelihoods;
translations.idiomatic: Finish roughly what is already underway so court ceremonies can proceed, then halt all new work and let the people return to their fields;

sentences.zh: 二方平定，復可徐興。

translations.literal: when the two regions are pacified, construction may slowly be resumed.
translations.idiomatic: when both enemies are subdued, building may resume at leisure.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》：天子后妃以下百二十人，嬪嬙之儀，既已盛矣。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou: for the Son of Heaven, empress and consorts below numbered one hundred twenty—the protocol for concubines and attendants was already ample.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou allot the Son of Heaven one empress and consorts below her, one hundred twenty in all—the protocol for palace women is already ample.

sentences.zh: 竊聞後庭之數，或復過之，聖嗣不昌，殆能由此。

translations.literal: I have heard that the number in the rear court may again exceed this; the imperial heirs are not flourishing—perhaps it can be from this.
translations.idiomatic: I hear the rear apartments may exceed even that number; the lack of flourishing imperial heirs may stem from this.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為可妙簡淑媛以備內官之數，其餘盡遣還家，且以育精養神，專靜為寶。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly considers that you may finely select virtuous ladies to fill the inner offices' quota, send all the rest home, and thereby nurture essence and nourish spirit, taking quiet concentration as treasure.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly suggest selecting only the finest ladies to fill the prescribed inner ranks, sending all others home so Your Majesty may conserve your vitality and keep to stillness.

sentences.zh: 如此，則《螽斯》之征可庶而致矣。

translations.literal: If so, the omen of the "Locusts" may perhaps be attained.
translations.idiomatic: Then the blessing of many sons foretold in the "Locusts" ode may yet be realized.

sentences.zh: 」帝報曰：「卿輒昌言，他復以聞。

translations.literal: " The Emperor replied: "You are always speaking forthrightly; report again on other matters.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor answered, "You speak plainly as ever; bring me word of anything else.

sentences.zh: 」是時獵法嚴峻，殺禁地鹿者身死，財產沒官，有能覺告者，厚加賞賜。

translations.literal: " At this time hunting laws were severe: one who killed deer in forbidden ground was put to death and property confiscated for the state; whoever could detect and report received rich reward.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time hunting laws were harsh—killing deer in the imperial preserves was punishable by death and confiscation of property, with heavy rewards for informers.

sentences.zh: 柔復上疏曰：「中間以來，百姓供給眾役，親田者既減；

translations.literal: Rou again submitted a memorial saying: "Since the middle period the common people have supplied many corvées; those who personally tilled fields have already diminished;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rou memorialized again: "For some time the people have borne endless corvée; those who farm their own land grow fewer by the day;

sentences.zh: 加頃復有獵禁，群鹿犯暴，殘食生苗，處處為害，所傷不貲，民雖障離，力不能御。

translations.literal: moreover recently there is again the hunting ban—herds of deer commit outrages, ravaging and eating the young grain, harming everywhere, the damage beyond reckoning; though the people fence them off, they lack strength to repel them.
translations.idiomatic: and now the hunting ban lets deer overrun the fields, devouring the young grain everywhere at incalculable cost. The farmers fence them out but cannot hold them back.

sentences.zh: 至如滎陽左右，周數百里，歲略不收。

translations.literal: As for the area around Xingyang, for several hundred li in circuit, the year has scarcely any harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Around Xingyang, for hundreds of li in every direction, the year has brought almost no harvest.

sentences.zh: 方今天下生生者甚少，而麋鹿之損者甚多，卒有兵戎之役，凶年之災，將無以待之。

translations.literal: Just now those who live and thrive under Heaven are very few, while the harm from elk and deer is very great; if suddenly there should be military campaigns or years of disaster, there will be nothing to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Those who live and prosper under Heaven are few, while deer destroy far more—if war or famine should strike, what will we have to fall back on?

sentences.zh: 惟陛下寬放民間，使得捕鹿，遂除其禁，則眾庶永濟，莫不悅豫矣。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty broadly release the people, allow them to hunt deer, and remove the ban—then the multitude will be forever aided and none will not rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty relax the ban and let the people hunt deer—the common folk will be forever sustained, and all will rejoice.

sentences.zh: 」帝又欲平北芒，令於其上作台觀，望見孟津。

translations.literal: " The Emperor also wished to level the Northern Mang hills and build terraces and towers on them to see the Meng Ford.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor also wished to level the Northern Mang hills and erect terraces and towers from which to view the Meng Ford.

sentences.zh: 衛尉辛毘諫曰：「天地之性，高高下下。

translations.literal: Commandant of the Guards Xin Pi remonstrated, saying: "The nature of Heaven and Earth is high here, low there.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of the Guards Xin Pi remonstrated: "Heaven and Earth have their proper heights and depths.

sentences.zh: 今而反之，既非其理；

translations.literal: To reverse this now is already contrary to principle;
translations.idiomatic: To level them now runs against nature itself;

sentences.zh: 加以損費人功，民不堪役。

translations.literal: moreover it wastes human labor and the people cannot bear the corvée.
translations.idiomatic: and it wastes labor the people cannot endure.

sentences.zh: 且若九河盈溢，洪水為害，而丘陵皆夷，將何以御之！

translations.literal: Moreover, if the nine rivers overflow and flood waters do harm, while hills and mounds are all leveled, with what will you defend against them!
translations.idiomatic: If the nine rivers should flood and the hills are flattened, what barrier will remain!

sentences.zh: 」帝乃止。

translations.literal: " The Emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 少府楊阜上疏曰：「陛下奉武皇帝開拓之大業，守文皇帝克終之元緒，誠宜思齊往古聖賢之善治，總觀季世放蕩之惡政。

translations.literal: Privy Treasurer Yang Fu submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty inherits the great enterprise of expansion opened by Emperor Wu and the primal thread of completion guarded by the Cultured Emperor—you truly ought to think of matching the good governance of ancient sages and take in view the evil policies of the late age's dissipation.
translations.idiomatic: Privy Treasurer Yang Fu memorialized: "Your Majesty holds the great enterprise of expansion begun by Emperor Wu and the founding work brought to completion by the Cultured Emperor. You should strive to equal the sage rulers of old and take warning from the reckless policies of the dynasty's final years.

sentences.zh: 曩使桓、靈不廢高祖之法度，文、景之恭儉，太祖雖有神武，於何所施，而陛下何由處斯尊哉！

translations.literal: If formerly Huan and Ling had not abandoned the High Ancestor's laws and standards, and the reverence and frugality of Wen and Jing, even if the Founding Emperor had divine martial prowess, where could he have applied it—and how could Your Majesty occupy this exalted position!
translations.idiomatic: Had Emperors Huan and Ling not cast aside Gaozu's laws and the frugality of Wen and Jing, our founding emperor's martial genius would have had no field to prove itself—and how would Your Majesty sit upon this throne!

sentences.zh: 今吳、蜀未定，定旅在外，諸所繕治，惟陛下務從約節。

translations.literal: Now Wu and Shu are not settled and armies are abroad; in all repairs and constructions, may Your Majesty strive for economy and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Shu are not yet subdued and our armies are in the field—in all building and repair, may Your Majesty practice strict economy.

sentences.zh: 」帝優詔答之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor answered with an excellent edict.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 阜復上疏曰：「堯尚茅茨而萬國安其居，禹卑宮室而天下樂其業。

translations.literal: Fu again submitted a memorial saying: "Yao still used thatched huts and the ten thousand states were secure in their dwellings; Yu kept palaces lowly and all under Heaven rejoiced in their work.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu memorialized again: "Yao lived in thatched huts and the myriad states dwelt in peace; Yu kept his palaces humble and the world rejoiced in its labors.

sentences.zh: 及至殷、周，或堂崇三尺，度以九筵耳。

translations.literal: Down to Yin and Zhou, a hall might be three chi in height, measured by nine mats—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Even in Yin and Zhou, halls rose no more than three chi, their span measured in nine mats.

sentences.zh: 桀作璇室象廊，紂為傾宮鹿台，以喪其社稷；

translations.literal: Jie made the jade chamber and ivory corridor; Zhou made the tilting palace and deer tower—and lost their altars of soil and grain;
translations.idiomatic: Jie built the Jade Chamber and Ivory Corridor; Zhou built the Tilting Palace and Deer Tower—and both lost their realms;

sentences.zh: 楚靈以築章華而身受禍；

translations.literal: King Ling of Chu, by building Zhanghua, personally suffered disaster;
translations.idiomatic: King Ling of Chu built Zhanghua and brought disaster on himself;

sentences.zh: 秦始皇作阿房，二世而滅。

translations.literal: Qin Shihuang built Epang; in the second generation it perished.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang built Epang Palace; his line was extinguished in the second generation.

sentences.zh: 夫不度萬民之力，以從耳目之欲，未有不亡者也。

translations.literal: Those who do not measure the strength of the ten thousand people to follow the desires of eyes and ears—none have failed to perish.
translations.idiomatic: Those who spend the people's strength to gratify their senses have never failed to fall.

sentences.zh: 陛下當以堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武為法則，夏桀、殷紂、楚靈、秦皇為深誡，而乃自暇自逸，惟宮台是飾，必有顛覆危亡之禍矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought to take Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu as models, and Xia Jie, Yin Zhou, Chu Ling, and Qin Huang as deep warnings—yet you give yourself leisure and ease, adorning only palaces and towers; there will surely be the calamity of overthrow and peril.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should take Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu as your models, and Jie, Zhou, King Ling of Chu, and the First Emperor of Qin as solemn warnings—yet you indulge in ease and adorn only palaces and towers. Overthrow and ruin are sure to follow.

sentences.zh: 君作元首，臣為股肱，存亡一體，得失同之。

translations.literal: The ruler is the head, ministers are the arms and legs—survival and destruction are one body, gain and loss are shared.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler is the head and his ministers the arms and legs—survival and ruin are one body, and gain and loss are shared alike.

sentences.zh: 臣雖駑怯，敢忘爭臣之義！

translations.literal: Though your servant is dull and timid, how dare I forget the duty of a remonstrating minister!
translations.idiomatic: Though I am slow and timid, how dare I forget a loyal minister's duty to speak plainly!

sentences.zh: 言不切至，不足以感寤陛下。

translations.literal: If words are not cutting and direct, they are insufficient to awaken Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Words that are not blunt and urgent cannot move Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 陛下不察臣言，恐皇祖、烈考之祚墜於地。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not examine your servant's words, I fear the fortune of your imperial ancestors and illustrious father may fall to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will not heed me, I fear the throne of your imperial ancestors may fall to ruin.

sentences.zh: 使臣身死有補萬一，則死之日猶生之年也。

translations.literal: If your servant's death might avail one part in ten thousand, then the day of death would be like a year of life.
translations.idiomatic: If my death might avail even a little, the day I die would count as a day I lived.

sentences.zh: 謹叩棺沐浴，伏俟重誅！

translations.literal: I respectfully knock on my coffin and bathe, prostrate awaiting heavy punishment!
translations.idiomatic: I have prepared my coffin and bathed, and await Your Majesty's severest judgment!

sentences.zh: 」奏御，帝感其忠言，手筆詔答。

translations.literal: " When the memorial reached the throne, the Emperor was moved by his loyal words and answered with an edict in his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial reached him, the emperor was moved by Yang Fu's loyalty and answered in his own hand.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗著衣冒，被縹綾半袖。

translations.literal: The Emperor once wore a traveling cloak with light silk half-sleeves.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once wore a traveling cloak with light silk half-sleeves.

sentences.zh: 阜問帝曰：「此於禮何法服也？

translations.literal: Fu asked the Emperor: "By what rule of ritual is this garment?
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu asked, "What ritual garment is this?

sentences.zh: 」帝默然不答。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was silent and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 自是不法服不以見阜。

translations.literal: From then on he did not wear irregular garments when receiving Fu.
translations.idiomatic: After that he never received Yang Fu in improper dress.

sentences.zh: 阜又上疏欲省宮人諸不見幸者，乃召御府吏問後宮人數。

translations.literal: Fu again submitted a memorial wishing to reduce palace women who had not received favor; he then summoned an official of the Imperial Wardrobe to ask the number in the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu memorialized again to dismiss palace women who had never received the emperor's favor, and summoned an official of the Imperial Wardrobe to ask how many women were in the rear apartments.

sentences.zh: 吏守舊令，對曰：「禁密，不得宣露！

translations.literal: The official kept to the old order and replied: "It is forbidden and secret—it may not be disclosed!
translations.idiomatic: The clerk cited the old regulations: "That is secret—it may not be disclosed!

sentences.zh: 」阜怒，杖吏一百，數之曰：「國家不與九卿為密，反與小吏為密乎！

translations.literal: " Fu was angry, flogged the official one hundred strokes, and rebuked him, saying: "The state does not keep secrets from the Nine Ministers—does it keep secrets from petty clerks instead!
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Fu had him beaten a hundred strokes and rebuked him: "The state keeps no secrets from the Nine Ministers—must it keep them from petty clerks instead!

sentences.zh: 」帝愈嚴憚之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor came to fear him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor feared him all the more.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍蔣濟上疏曰：「昔句踐養胎以待用，昭王恤病以雪仇，故能以弱燕服強齊，羸越滅勁吳。

translations.literal: Regular Attendant Jiang Ji submitted a memorial saying: "In the past Goujian nourished his strength to await employment; King Zhao of Yan comforted the sick to avenge his grievance—thus they were able with weak Yan to subdue strong Qi, and with enfeebled Yue to destroy stalwart Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Regular Attendant Jiang Ji memorialized: "Goujian of Yue husbanded his strength until the time was ripe; King Zhao of Yan nursed the wounded to settle his score—thus weak Yan overcame mighty Qi, and exhausted Yue destroyed powerful Wu.

sentences.zh: 今二敵強盛，當身不除，百世之責也。

translations.literal: Now the two foes are powerful and flourishing; if not removed in your own person, it is a responsibility for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Our two enemies are strong today; if they are not destroyed in Your Majesty's lifetime, the blame will fall on a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 以陛下聖明神武之略，捨其緩者，專心討賊，臣以為無難矣。

translations.literal: With Your Majesty's sagely clarity and divine martial strategy, if you set aside what is slow and focus your mind on punishing the rebels, your servant considers there would be no difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's sagacity and martial prowess, if you set aside lesser matters and concentrate on destroying the enemy, I see no difficulty at all.

sentences.zh: 」中書侍郎東萊王基上疏曰：「臣聞古人以水喻民曰：『水所以載舟，亦所以覆舟。

translations.literal: The Zhongshu Vice Director Wang Ji of Donglai submitted a memorial, saying: "Your subject has heard that the ancients used water as a metaphor for the people, saying: 'Water is what carries the boat, and it is also what capsizes the boat.'
translations.idiomatic: The Zhongshu Vice Director Wang Ji of Donglai submitted a memorial, saying, "I have heard that the ancients likened the people to water, saying, 'Water is what carries the boat—and it is also what capsizes it.'

sentences.zh: 』顏淵曰『東野子之御，馬力盡矣，而求進不已，殆將敗矣。

translations.literal: Yan Yuan said: 'In Dongyezi's driving, the horses' strength is already exhausted, yet he still seeks to advance without stopping; he is on the verge of ruin.'
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yuan said, "In Dongyezi's driving, the horses' strength is already spent, yet he still presses onward without cease—he is on the verge of ruin."

sentences.zh: 』今事役勞苦，男女離曠，願陛下深察東野之敝，留意舟水之喻，息奔駟於未盡，節力役於未困。

translations.literal: Now corvée labor is arduous, and men and women are separated and estranged. I hope Your Majesty will deeply examine the harm of Dongye's driving, take heed of the boat-and-water metaphor, halt the galloping horses before they are spent, and limit forced labor before the people are exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée labor is now grueling, and men and women are torn apart and left alone. I beg Your Majesty to look closely at the harm in Dongye's driving, keep in mind the lesson of boat and water, stop the galloping team before their strength is gone, and curb forced labor before the people are worn down.

sentences.zh: 昔漢有天下，至孝文時唯有同姓諸侯，而賈誼憂之曰：『置火積薪之下而寢其上，因謂之安。

translations.literal: In the past, when Han possessed the realm, by the time of Emperor Xiaowen there were only feudal lords of the same surname, yet Jia Yi worried and said: 'To place fire beneath a pile of kindling and sleep upon it, and thereby call it safe.'
translations.idiomatic: In the past, when Han held the realm, by the reign of Emperor Xiaowen there were only feudal lords of the imperial surname—yet Jia Yi still worried and said, 'To pile firewood, lay a fire beneath it, sleep on top, and call that safe.'

sentences.zh: 』今寇賊未殄，猛將擁兵，檢之則無以應敵，久之則難以遺後，當盛明之世，不務以除患，若子孫不競，社稷之憂也。

translations.literal: Now the bandits and rebels are not yet eliminated, and fierce generals hold armies in their grasp. If one inspects and reduces them, there is no means to respond to the enemy; if one keeps them too long, it is hard to leave the problem to posterity. In this flourishing and enlightened age, if you do not strive to remove calamities, and if your descendants are not vigorous, it will be a worry for the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Today the bandits and rebels are not yet destroyed, and powerful generals hold armies in their hands. Restrain them, and you cannot meet the enemy; leave them too long, and you cannot safely bequeath the realm to posterity. In this age of splendor and enlightenment, if you do not strive to remove these dangers—and if your descendants prove unequal to the task—it will be a calamity for the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 使賈誼復起，必深切於曩時矣。

translations.literal: If Jia Yi were to rise again, he would surely be even more deeply concerned than in former times.
translations.idiomatic: If Jia Yi were to rise again, his alarm would surely run even deeper than before.

sentences.zh: 」帝皆不聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not heed any of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed any of it.

sentences.zh: 殿中監督役，擅收蘭台令史，右僕射衛臻奏案之。

translations.literal: The supervisor of palace construction forcibly seized a Lantai clerk; Right Vice Director Wei Zhen memorialized to investigate the case.
translations.idiomatic: The supervisor of palace construction forcibly detained a Lantai clerk; the Right Vice Director Wei Zhen memorialized requesting that the case be investigated.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「殿捨不成，吾所留心，卿推之，何也？

translations.literal: An edict said: "The palace buildings are not finished—this is what concerns me. Why do you press the case?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said by edict, "The palace buildings are not yet finished—that is what weighs on my mind. Why are you pressing this case?"

sentences.zh: 」臻曰：「古制侵官之法，非惡其勤事也，誠以所益者小，所墮者大也。

translations.literal: Zhen said: "The ancient regulation on encroaching upon another's office was not made because one hates diligence in affairs; it is truly because what is gained is small, while what is ruined is great."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhen replied, "The ancient law against overstepping office was not made because diligence in affairs is hated; it is because what is gained is small, while what is lost is great."

sentences.zh: 臣每察校事，類皆如此，若又縱之，懼群司將遂越職，以至陵夷矣。

translations.literal: Whenever I examine matters of this sort, they are all like this. If this is indulged again, I fear the various bureaus will gradually overstep their duties, until government declines.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I examine such matters, they are all of this kind. If this is indulged again, I fear the various offices will go on overstepping their duties until government itself declines.

sentences.zh: 尚書涿郡孫禮固請罷役，帝詔曰：「欽納讜言。

translations.literal: Minister of the Masters Sun Li of Zhuo Commandery repeatedly requested that corvée be stopped. The Emperor issued an edict saying: "I respectfully accept your forthright counsel."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Li, Minister of the Masters, from Zhuo Commandery, repeatedly petitioned to halt corvée labor. The emperor issued an edict saying, "I respectfully accept your forthright counsel."

sentences.zh: 」促遣民作；

translations.literal: " He urgently ordered the people dismissed from labor;
translations.idiomatic: " He urgently ordered the corvée workers sent home;

sentences.zh: 監作者復奏留一月，有所成訖。

translations.literal: the construction supervisors again memorialized to retain them for one month until some work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: the construction supervisors again memorialized asking to keep them one month more until certain work was finished.

sentences.zh: 禮徑至作所，不復重奏，稱詔罷民，帝奇其意而不責。

translations.literal: Sun Li went directly to the work site, without submitting another memorial, and announced the edict dismissing the people; the Emperor admired his intent and did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Li went straight to the work site without submitting another memorial, announced the edict dismissing the people, and the emperor admired his resolve and did not reproach him.

sentences.zh: 帝雖不能盡用群臣直諫之言，然皆優容之。

translations.literal: Although the Emperor could not fully adopt the frank remonstrances of his ministers, he nevertheless treated them all with generous forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Although the emperor could not fully act on his ministers' frank remonstrances, he nevertheless received them all with generous forbearance.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，洛陽崇華殿災。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Chonghua Hall in Luoyang was destroyed by fire.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Chonghua Hall in Luoyang burned down.

sentences.zh: 帝問侍中領太史令泰山高堂隆曰：「此何咎也？

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Palace Attendant and Acting Director of the Imperial Astronomers Gao Tanglong of Taishan: "What blame is this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the Palace Attendant and Acting Director of the Imperial Astronomers, Gao Tanglong of Taishan, "What fault does this signify?"

sentences.zh: 於禮寧有祈禳之義乎？

translations.literal: Is there in ritual perhaps the meaning of offering prayers to avert calamity?"
translations.idiomatic: Does ritual provide any grounds for prayers of supplication and expiation?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「《易‧傳》曰：『上不儉，下不節，孽火燒其室。

translations.literal: He replied: "The Commentary on the Changes says: 'When those above are not frugal and those below are not restrained, baleful fire burns their house.'"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The Commentary on the Changes says, 'When those above are not frugal and those below are not restrained, baleful fire burns their house.'"

sentences.zh: 』又曰：『君高其台，天火為災。

translations.literal: It also says: 'When the ruler raises his terraces high, heaven's fire becomes a calamity.'"
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "When the ruler raises his terraces high, heaven's fire becomes a calamity."

sentences.zh: 』此人君務飾宮室，不知百姓空竭，故天應之以旱，火從高殿起也。

translations.literal: This means the ruler strives to adorn the palaces, unaware that the common people are emptied and exhausted; therefore Heaven responded with drought, and fire arose from the high hall."
translations.idiomatic: This means the ruler busies himself adorning the palace, heedless that the common people are drained and exhausted—so Heaven answered with drought, and fire broke out from the high hall."

sentences.zh: 」詔問隆：「吾聞漢武帝之時柏梁災，而大起宮殿以厭之，其義雲何？

translations.literal: An edict asked Long: "I have heard that in the time of Emperor Wu of Han, the Boling Hall burned, and he greatly raised palaces to suppress it—what is the meaning of this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Long by edict, "I have heard that in Emperor Wu of Han's time the Boling Hall burned, and he thereupon built palaces on a grand scale to suppress the omen—what is the meaning of that?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「夷越之巫所為，非聖賢之明訓也。

translations.literal: He replied: "That was the doing of Yue and barbarian shamans; it is not the bright teaching of sages and worthies."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "That was the work of Yue and barbarian shamans—it is not the enlightened teaching of sages and worthies."

sentences.zh: 《五行志》曰：『柏梁災，其後有江充巫蠱事。

translations.literal: The Records of the Five Phases says: 'When Boling burned, afterward came the Jiang Chong witchcraft affair.'"
translations.idiomatic: The Records of the Five Phases says, "When Boling burned, the affair of Jiang Chong's witchcraft followed."

sentences.zh: 』如《志》之言，越巫建章無所厭也。

translations.literal: According to the Records, building Zhang Hall did nothing to suppress the omen.
translations.idiomatic: As the Records say, the Yue shamans' building of Zhang Hall did nothing to suppress the omen.

sentences.zh: 令宜罷散民役。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should dismiss the corvée laborers.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should now dismiss the corvée laborers.

sentences.zh: 宮室之制，務從約節，清掃所災之處，不敢於此有所立作，則萐莆、嘉禾必生此地。

translations.literal: In palace construction, let everything be kept simple and restrained; sweep clean the burned ground and build nothing new upon it—then ten-thousand-leaf grass and auspicious grain will spring up there.
translations.idiomatic: In palace construction, let everything be kept simple and restrained; sweep clean the burned ground and build nothing new upon it—then ten-thousand-leaf grass and auspicious grain will spring up there.

sentences.zh: 若乃疲民之力，竭民之財，非所以致符瑞而懷遠人也。

translations.literal: To wear out the people's strength and drain their wealth is no way to summon auspicious omens or win over distant peoples.
translations.idiomatic: To wear out the people's strength and drain their wealth is no way to summon auspicious omens or win over distant peoples.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚午，立皇子芳為齊王，詢為秦王。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on day Gengwu, Prince Fang was enfeoffed as Prince of Qi and Prince Xun as Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day gengwu, Prince Fang was enfeoffed as Prince of Qi and Prince Xun as Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 帝無子，養二王為子，宮省事秘，莫有知其所由來者。

translations.literal: The Emperor had no sons of his own and adopted the two princes—the palace kept the matter secret, and none knew their origins.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no sons of his own and adopted the two princes as his own; the palace kept the matter secret, and no one knew their origins.

sentences.zh: 或云：芳，任城王楷之子也。

translations.literal: Some say Prince Fang was the son of Prince Kai of Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Some said that Fang was the son of Prince Kai of Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，帝還洛陽。

translations.literal: On day Dingsi, the Emperor returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingsi, the emperor returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 詔復立崇華殿，更名曰九龍。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chonghua Hall rebuilt and renamed Nine Dragons Hall.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Chonghua Hall rebuilt and renamed Nine Dragons Hall.

sentences.zh: 通引穀水過九龍殿前，為玉井綺欄，蟾蜍含受，神龍吐出。

translations.literal: The Gu River was diverted to flow before Nine Dragons Hall, with jade wells and ornate railings fashioned so that toads received the water and divine dragons spouted it forth.
translations.idiomatic: The Gu River was diverted to flow before Nine Dragons Hall, with jade wells and ornate railings fashioned so that toads received the water and divine dragons spouted it forth.

sentences.zh: 使博士扶風馬鈞作司南車，水轉百戲。

translations.literal: He had the Erudite Ma Jun of Fufeng construct a south-pointing chariot and water-driven mechanical entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He had the Erudite Ma Jun of Fufeng construct a south-pointing chariot and water-driven mechanical entertainments.

sentences.zh: 陵霄闕始構，有鵲巢其上，帝以問高堂隆，對曰：「《詩》曰：『惟鵲有巢，惟鳩居之。

translations.literal: When Lingxiao Gate was first under construction and magpies built nests upon it, the Emperor asked Gao Tanglong about it; he replied: "The Book of Songs says, 'The magpie has its nest; the turtledove dwells in it.'"
translations.idiomatic: When Lingxiao Gate was first under construction and magpies built nests upon it, the emperor asked Gao Tanglong about it; he replied, "The Book of Songs says, 'The magpie has its nest; the turtledove dwells in it.'"

sentences.zh: 』今興宮室，起陵霄闕，而鵲巢之，此宮未成身不得居之象也。

translations.literal: Now, as palace construction rises and Lingxiao Gate is built, magpies nest upon it—this is an image of the palace unfinished while its occupant cannot yet dwell within.
translations.idiomatic: Now, as palace construction rises and Lingxiao Gate is built, magpies nest upon it—this is an image of the palace unfinished while its occupant cannot yet dwell within.

sentences.zh: 大意若曰：『宮室未成，將有他姓制御之』。

translations.literal: Taken broadly, it is as if to say, 'The palace is not yet finished, and another surname will come to control it.'
translations.idiomatic: Taken broadly, it is as if to say, 'The palace is not yet finished, and another surname will come to control it.'

sentences.zh: 斯乃上天之戒也。

translations.literal: This is a warning sent down from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: This is a warning sent down from Heaven.

sentences.zh: 夫天道無親，惟與善人，太戊、武丁睹災悚懼，故天降之福。

translations.literal: Heaven is impartial and aids the good alone. Ta Yi and Wu Ding, when they saw calamity, were filled with dread—therefore Heaven bestowed blessings upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is impartial and aids the good alone. Ta Yi and Wu Ding, when they saw calamity, were filled with dread—therefore Heaven bestowed blessings upon them.

sentences.zh: 今若休罷百役，增崇德政，則三王可四，五帝可六，豈惟商宗轉禍為福而已哉！

translations.literal: If Your Majesty now halts the hundred corvées and elevates virtuous governance, you may match the Three Dynasties and surpass the Five Emperors—how much more than merely turning misfortune to fortune, as the Shang ruler did!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty now halts the hundred corvées and elevates virtuous governance, you may match the Three Dynasties and surpass the Five Emperors—how much more than merely turning misfortune to fortune, as the Shang ruler did!

sentences.zh: 」帝為之動容。

translations.literal: The Emperor was visibly moved by this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was visibly moved by this.

sentences.zh: 帝性嚴急，其督修宮室有稽限者，帝親召問，言猶在口，身首已分。

translations.literal: The Emperor's nature was stern and impatient; when those supervising palace construction fell behind schedule, he would summon them personally—and even as the words were still on his lips, head and body were already parted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's nature was stern and impatient; when those supervising palace construction fell behind schedule, he would summon them personally—and even as the words were still on his lips, head and body were already parted.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍領秘書監王肅上疏曰：「今宮室未就，見作者三四萬人。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant and Secretary Supervisor Wang Su submitted a memorial, saying: "The palace is not yet finished, and I see thirty or forty thousand workers on the site."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant and Secretary Supervisor Wang Su submitted a memorial, saying, "The palace is not yet finished, and I see thirty or forty thousand workers on the site."

sentences.zh: 九龍可以安聖體，其內足以列六宮；

translations.literal: Nine Dragons Hall can already accommodate Your Majesty's sacred person; within it there is room enough for the six palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Nine Dragons Hall can already accommodate Your Majesty's sacred person; within it there is room enough for the six palaces.

sentences.zh: 惟泰極已前，功夫尚大。

translations.literal: Only the work before Taiji Gate still requires great labor.
translations.idiomatic: Only the work before Taiji Gate still requires great labor.

sentences.zh: 願陛下取常食稟之士，非急要者之用，選其丁壯，擇留萬人，使一期而更之。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to take men from the regular grain-ration troops who are not urgently needed elsewhere, select the strongest among them, keep ten thousand, and rotate them at fixed intervals.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to take men from the regular grain-ration troops who are not urgently needed elsewhere, select the strongest among them, keep ten thousand, and rotate them at fixed intervals.

sentences.zh: 咸知息代有日，則莫不悅以即事，勞而不怨矣。

translations.literal: All knowing that relief and replacement have a fixed day, then none would not gladly take up the work, toiling yet without resentment.
translations.idiomatic: If every man knew the day when his turn would end, each would gladly set to work—laboring hard, yet without bitterness.

sentences.zh: 計一歲有三百六十萬夫，亦不為少。

translations.literal: Counting one year's labor, there are three million six hundred thousand man-days—it is not a small number.
translations.idiomatic: Count the labor for a full year, and it comes to three million six hundred thousand man-days—not a trifling sum.

sentences.zh: 當一歲成者，聽且三年，分遣其餘，使皆即農，無窮之計也。

translations.literal: Where one year's work would suffice, allow three years instead; send the rest away in rotation so that all may return at once to farming—a plan that never exhausts the people.
translations.idiomatic: Where a task could be finished in a year, stretch it across three; rotate the rest home in turn so that all may return to the fields at once—a policy that need never run dry.

sentences.zh: 夫信之於民，國家大寶也。

translations.literal: Now, trustworthiness toward the people is the great treasure of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Trust in the eyes of the people is the state's greatest treasure.

sentences.zh: 前車駕當幸洛陽，發民為營，有司命以營成而罷；

translations.literal: On a previous imperial progress, when Your Majesty was about to visit Luoyang, the people were mobilized for construction; the responsible officials ordered that they be dismissed once the work was complete;
translations.idiomatic: On an earlier progress, when Your Majesty was bound for Luoyang, commoners were conscripted for construction, and the responsible officials promised they would be released once the camps were finished;

sentences.zh: 既成，又利其功力，不以時遣。

translations.literal: once it was finished, they again coveted their labor and did not send them away on time.
translations.idiomatic: yet when the work was done, those in charge coveted their labor still and did not dismiss them when promised.

sentences.zh: 有司徒營目前之利，不顧經國之體。

translations.literal: There were ministers who sought immediate profit and gave no thought to the enduring structure of statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: Some ministers chased profit before their eyes and gave no thought to the enduring foundations of government.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為自今已後，儻復使民，宜明其令，使必如期，以次有事，寧使更發，無或失信。

translations.literal: Your servant is dull enough to think that from this day forward, if the people are conscripted again, the order should be made explicit and dismissal must come exactly on schedule; when further work arises, it would be better to conscript anew than ever to break faith.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly believe that hereafter, whenever the people are conscripted again, the command should be made explicit and release must come exactly as promised; when new tasks arise, it is better to levy fresh labor than ever to break faith.

sentences.zh: 凡陛下臨時之所行刑，皆有罪之吏、宜死之人也；

translations.literal: All executions Your Majesty carries out on the spot involve guilty officials who deserve death;
translations.idiomatic: Every execution Your Majesty orders on the spot involves officials who have committed crimes and men who deserve to die;

sentences.zh: 然眾庶不知，謂為倉卒。

translations.literal: yet the multitude does not know this and takes it for hasty, arbitrary killing.
translations.idiomatic: yet the common people do not know this, and believe you act in sudden, arbitrary wrath.

sentences.zh: 故願陛下下之於吏，而暴其罪，鈞其死也，無使污於宮掖而為遠近所疑。

translations.literal: Therefore I beg Your Majesty to hand such cases down to the officials, expose the culprit's crimes, and weigh the justice of his death, so that blood is not shed within the palace women's quarters and the court is not suspected by near and far.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore beg Your Majesty to refer such cases to the proper officials, make the culprit's crimes public, and let the justice of the sentence be weighed—so that blood is not shed within the inner palace and the throne is not suspect in the eyes of near and far.

sentences.zh: 且人命至重，難生易殺，氣絕不續者也，是以聖賢重之。

translations.literal: Moreover, human life is of the utmost weight: hard to restore once lost, easy to destroy, and once breath is cut off it cannot be resumed—therefore sages and worthies hold it in the highest regard.
translations.idiomatic: Human life is the weightiest thing of all: hard to give back, easy to take away, and once breath is severed it cannot be restored. That is why sages and worthies hold it sacred.

sentences.zh: 昔漢文帝欲殺犯蹕者，廷尉張釋之曰：『方其時，上使誅之則已，今下廷尉，廷尉，天下之平，不可傾也。

translations.literal: Formerly, when Emperor Wen of Han wished to put to death a man who had violated the imperial progress, the Court Commandant Zhang Shizhi said: "At that moment, if Your Majesty had ordered his execution, so be it; but now that the case has been sent down to the Court Commandant—the Court Commandant is the scale of all under Heaven, and that scale must not be tipped."
translations.idiomatic: In the past, when Emperor Wen of Han wished to execute a man who had violated the imperial progress, Court Commandant Zhang Shizhi said: "At that moment, had Your Majesty ordered his death, so be it; but now that the case has been sent down to me—the Court Commandant is the scale of the realm, and that scale must not be tipped."

sentences.zh: 』臣以為大失其義，非忠臣所宜陳也。

translations.literal: Your servant considers this a grave failure of principle—not what a loyal minister ought to say.
translations.idiomatic: I consider that a grave failure of principle—not what a loyal minister ought to say.

sentences.zh: 廷尉者，天子之吏也，猶不可以失平，而天子之身反可以惑謬乎！

translations.literal: The Court Commandant is the Son of Heaven's own officer; even he may not lose impartiality—how then can the Son of Heaven's own person be indulged in confusion and error!
translations.idiomatic: The Court Commandant is the emperor's own officer; even he may not lose his balance—how then can the emperor's own person be allowed to err in judgment!

sentences.zh: 斯重於為己而輕於為君，不忠之甚也，不可不察！

translations.literal: This is to weigh one's own interest heavily and the lord's lightly—the depth of disloyalty; it cannot go unexamined!
translations.idiomatic: That is to weigh one's own interest heavily and the ruler's lightly—the depth of disloyalty, and it must not pass unexamined!

sentences.zh: 中山恭王兗疾病，令官屬曰：「男子不死於婦人之手，亟以時營東堂。

translations.literal: Prince Gong of Zhongshan, Cao Gun, fell ill and ordered his staff, saying: "A man should not die in a woman's hands—build the Eastern Hall at once, and on time."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gong of Zhongshan, Cao Gun, fell gravely ill and told his officials: "A man should not die in a woman's hands—build the Eastern Hall at once, and see that it is finished on time."

sentences.zh: 」堂成，輿疾往居之。

translations.literal: When the hall was complete, he had himself carried there ill to dwell in it.
translations.idiomatic: When the hall was finished, he had himself carried there, sick as he was, and took up residence in it.

sentences.zh: 又令世子曰：「汝幼為人君，知樂不知苦，必將以驕奢為失者也。

translations.literal: He further charged his heir, saying: "You are young in your rule; you know pleasure but not hardship, and will surely take pride and extravagance for your ruin."
translations.idiomatic: He also charged his heir: "You are young on the throne; you know pleasure but not hardship, and will surely take pride and luxury for your downfall."

sentences.zh: 兄弟有不良之行，當造膝諫之，諫之不從，流涕喻之，喻之不改，乃白其母，猶不改，當以奏聞，並辭國土。

translations.literal: If your brothers commit unworthy conduct, you should admonish them face to face; if they do not heed you, plead with them through tears; if they still do not change, then tell your mother; if they still do not change, you should report it to the throne and resign your fief together with them.
translations.idiomatic: If any of your brothers commit unworthy acts, admonish them at close quarters; if they will not listen, plead with tears; if they still do not mend, tell your mother; if they still will not mend, report the matter to the throne and surrender your fief together with them.

sentences.zh: 與其守寵罹禍，不若貧賤全身也。

translations.literal: Better to live in poverty and low estate with one's body intact than to cling to favor and court disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Better to live poor and obscure with one's life whole than to cling to royal favor and invite ruin.

sentences.zh: 此亦謂大罪惡耳，其微過細故，當掩覆之。

translations.literal: This applies only to grave crimes and wickedness; as for minor faults and small matters, you should cover them over.
translations.idiomatic: This applies only to great crimes and wickedness; minor faults and small slips should be covered over.

sentences.zh: 」冬，十月，己酉，袞卒。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day Jiyou, Gun died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the day jiyou, Gun died.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁酉，帝行如許昌。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day Dingyou, the emperor traveled to Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day dingyou, the emperor traveled to Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 是歲，幽州刺史王雄使勇士韓龍刺殺鮮卑軻比能。

translations.literal: That year, Wang Xiong, governor of You Province, sent the warrior Han Long to assassinate Kebineng of the Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Wang Xiong, governor of You Province, sent the warrior Han Long to assassinate Kebineng of the Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 自是種落離散，互相侵伐，強者遠遁，弱者請服，邊陲遂安。

translations.literal: From this the tribes scattered, raided one another, the strong fled far away, the weak submitted, and the frontier was thereafter at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the tribes broke apart and raided one another; the strong fled far off, the weak submitted, and the borderlands were at last quiet.

sentences.zh: 張掖柳谷口水溢湧，寶石負圖，狀象靈龜，立於川西，有石馬七及鳳皇、麒麟、白虎、犧牛、璜玦、八卦、列宿、孛彗之象，又有文曰「大討曹」。

translations.literal: At Liugu in Zhangye commandery the waters overflowed and surged; a precious stone bearing a chart emerged, shaped like a numinous tortoise, standing west of the river. There were images of seven stone horses, the phoenix, the qilin, the white tiger, the sacrificial ox, jade pendants and rings, the Eight Trigrams, the constellations, and comets, and an inscription reading "Great chastisement of Cao."
translations.idiomatic: At Liugu in Zhangye, floodwaters burst forth and a precious stone bearing a chart emerged, shaped like a numinous tortoise, standing on the west bank of the river. It bore images of seven stone horses, the phoenix, the qilin, the white tiger, the sacrificial ox, jade pendants and rings, the Eight Trigrams, the constellations, and comets, along with an inscription reading "Great chastisement of Cao."

sentences.zh: 詔書班天下，以為嘉瑞。

translations.literal: An imperial edict was promulgated throughout the realm, treating it as an auspicious omen.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict was promulgated throughout the realm, proclaiming it an auspicious portent.

sentences.zh: 任令於綽連繼以問巨鹿張□，□密謂綽曰：「夫神以知來，不追已往，祥兆先見，而後廢興從之。

translations.literal: Magistrate Ren Ling Yu Chuo relayed the matter in turn to Zhang Mi of Julu, and Zhang Mi said to Chuo: "The divine knows what is to come and does not chase what is already past; auspicious signs appear first, and rise and fall follow after."
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Ren Ling Yu Chuo relayed the matter in turn to Zhang Mi of Julu, and Zhang Mi told Chuo: "The divine foreknows what is to come and does not chase what is already past; auspicious signs appear first, and only then do dynasties rise and fall."

sentences.zh: 今漢已久亡，魏已得之，何所追興祥兆乎！

translations.literal: Now Han has long perished and Wei has already taken the realm—why chase after omens to restore Han!
translations.idiomatic: Han has long since perished and Wei already holds the realm—why would one chase omens to restore Han!

sentences.zh: 此石，當今之變異而將來之符瑞也。

translations.literal: This stone is a portent of change in the present age and a token of fortune yet to come.
translations.idiomatic: This stone is a sign of change in the present age and a token of fortune yet to come.

sentences.zh: 帝使人以馬易珠璣、悲翠、玳瑁於吳，吳主曰：「此皆孤所不用，而可以得馬，孤何愛焉。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to trade horses with Wu for pearls, jadeite, and tortoise shell; the ruler of Wu said: "These are things I have no use for, yet they can win me horses—why should I begrudge them?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to trade horses with Wu for pearls, jadeite, and tortoise shell; the ruler of Wu said, "These are things I have no use for, yet they can win me horses—why should I begrudge them?"

sentences.zh: 」皆以與之。

translations.literal: He gave them all.
translations.idiomatic: He gave them all.

sentences.zh: 烈祖明皇帝中之下青龍四年（

translations.literal: Illustrious Ancestor Emperor Ming, middle scroll, lower part, Qinglong year four (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming the Illustrious Ancestor, Part Two (conclusion), Qinglong year 4 (

sentences.zh: 丙辰，公元二三六年）

translations.literal: Bingchen, the year 236 of the Common Era)
translations.idiomatic: bingchen cycle, AD 236)

sentences.zh: 春，吳人鑄大錢，一當五百。

translations.literal: In spring, the people of Wu cast large coins, each worth five hundred of the standard coin.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, Wu cast heavy coins, each worth five hundred of the standard coin.

sentences.zh: 三月，吳張昭卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: In the third month, Zhang Zhao of Wu died at the age of eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Zhang Zhao of Wu died at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 昭容貌矜嚴，有威風，吳主以下，舉邦憚之。

translations.literal: Zhao's bearing was stern and dignified, with an air of authority; from the ruler of Wu down, the whole state stood in awe of him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's bearing was stern and dignified, with an air of commanding authority; from the ruler of Wu down, the whole state stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，漢主至湔，登觀阪，觀汶水之流，旬日而還。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the ruler of Han reached Jian, ascended Guanban, and gazed upon the flow of the Wen River; after ten days he returned.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, the ruler of Han reached Jian, climbed Guanban, and watched the Wen River flow; after ten days he returned.

sentences.zh: 武都氐王符健請降於漢；

translations.literal: Fu Jian, Di king of Wudu, requested surrender to Han;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian, Di king of Wudu, asked to surrender to Han;

sentences.zh: 其弟不從，將四百戶來降。

translations.literal: his younger brother would not follow him and instead led four hundred households to come over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: his younger brother refused, and led four hundred households to come over in surrender.

sentences.zh: 五月，乙卯，樂平定侯董昭卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day Yimao, Dong Zhao, Marquis of Leipingding, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day yimao, Dong Zhao, Marquis of Leipingding, died.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己卯，帝還洛陽宮。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day Jimao, the emperor returned to the Luoyang palace.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the day jimao, the emperor returned to the Luoyang palace.

sentences.zh: 甲申，有星孛於大辰，又勃於東方。

translations.literal: On the day Jiashen, a comet appeared at Dachen, and blazed again in the east.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiashen, a comet appeared at Dachen, and blazed again in the east.

sentences.zh: 高堂隆上疏曰：「凡帝王徙都立邑，皆先定天地、社稷之位，敬恭以奉之。

translations.literal: Gao Tanglong submitted a memorial, saying: "Whenever emperors move the capital and establish a city, they first fix the positions of Heaven and Earth and the altars of soil and grain, and reverently attend to them."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Tanglong submitted a memorial, saying, "Whenever an emperor moves the capital and establishes a city, he first fixes the positions of Heaven and Earth and the altars of soil and grain, and reverently attends to them."

sentences.zh: 將營宮室，則宗廟為先，廄庫為次，居室為後。

translations.literal: When palace halls are to be built, the ancestral temple comes first, the stables and storehouses next, and the living quarters last.
translations.idiomatic: When palace halls are to be built, the ancestral temple comes first, the stables and storehouses next, and the living quarters last.

sentences.zh: 今圜丘、方澤、南北郊、明堂、社稷神位未定，宗廟之制又未如禮，而崇飾居室，士民失業，外人鹹云『宮人之用與軍國之費略齊』，民不堪命，皆有怨怒。

translations.literal: Now the Round Mound, the Square Pond, the southern and northern suburban altars, the Bright Hall, and the spirit-seats of the altars of soil and grain are still unfixed; the regulations for the ancestral temple still fall short of ritual propriety; yet you lavish ornament upon the living quarters, scholars and commoners lose their livelihood, and outsiders all say, "The cost of the palace women nearly equals the expense of army and state," until the people can no longer bear their burdens and anger fills the land.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Round Mound, the Square Pond, the southern and northern suburban altars, the Bright Hall, and the spirit-seats of the altars of soil and grain remain unfixed; the ancestral temple still falls short of ritual propriety; yet you lavish ornament upon the living quarters, scholars and commoners lose their livelihood, and outsiders all say, "The cost of the palace women nearly equals the expense of army and state," until the people can no longer bear their burdens and wrath fills the land.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：『天聰明自我民聰明，天明畏自我民明威。

translations.literal: The Documents says: "Heaven is clear-sighted because we the people are clear-sighted; Heaven's bright awe comes from we the people's bright awe."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says, "Heaven is clear-sighted because we the people are clear-sighted; Heaven's bright awe comes from we the people's bright awe."

sentences.zh: 』言天之賞罰，隨民言，順民心也。

translations.literal: This means that Heaven's rewards and punishments follow what the people say and accord with the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: This means that Heaven's rewards and punishments follow what the people say and accord with the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 夫采椽、卑宮，唐、虞、大禹之所以垂皇風也；

translations.literal: Plain rafters and low halls—this is how Tang, Yu, and Great Yu left their imperial example to posterity;
translations.idiomatic: Plain rafters and low halls—this is how the rulers of Tang and Yu and Great Yu left their imperial example to posterity;

sentences.zh: 玉台、瓊室，夏癸、商辛之所以犯昊天也。

translations.literal: Jade terraces and jade chambers—this is how Jie of Xia and Xin of Shang offended August Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Jade terraces and jade chambers—this is how Jie of Xia and Zhou of Shang offended August Heaven.

sentences.zh: 今宮室過盛，天彗章灼，斯乃慈父懇切之訓。

translations.literal: Now the palace halls are excessive, and Heaven's comet blazes forth—this is a father's earnest and urgent admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Now the palace halls are excessive, and Heaven's comet blazes forth—this is a father's earnest and urgent admonition.

sentences.zh: 當崇孝子祗聳之禮，不宜有忽，以重天怒。

translations.literal: You ought to honor the reverent conduct of a filial son, and must not neglect it, lest Heaven's wrath be redoubled.
translations.idiomatic: You ought to honor the reverent conduct of a filial son, and must not neglect it, lest Heaven's wrath be redoubled.

sentences.zh: 」隆數切諫，帝頗不悅。

translations.literal: " Tanglong remonstrated repeatedly and sharply, and the emperor was quite displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Tanglong remonstrated repeatedly and sharply, and the emperor was quite displeased.

sentences.zh: 侍中盧毓進曰：「臣聞君明則臣直，古之聖王惟恐不聞其過，此乃臣等所以不及隆也。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant Lu Yu stepped forward and said: "I have heard that when the ruler is enlightened, his ministers are upright. The sage kings of old feared only that they might not hear of their faults—this is why we your ministers fall short of Tanglong."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant Lu Yu stepped forward and said, "I have heard that when the ruler is enlightened, his ministers are upright. The sage kings of old feared only that they might not hear of their faults—this is why we your ministers fall short of Tanglong."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃解。

translations.literal: " The emperor's mood then eased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mood then eased.

sentences.zh: 毓，植之子也。

translations.literal: Yu was the son of Lu Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was the son of Lu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 十二月，癸巳，穎陰靖侯陳群卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day Guisi, Chen Qun, Marquis of Yingyin, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day guisi, Chen Qun, Marquis of Yingyin, died.

sentences.zh: 群前後數陳得失，每上封事，輒削其草，時人及其子弟莫能知也。

translations.literal: Qun had repeatedly set forth what was right and wrong in affairs of state; each time he submitted a sealed memorial, he would destroy the draft, so that neither his contemporaries nor his own sons and younger relatives could know what he had written.
translations.idiomatic: Qun had repeatedly set forth what was right and wrong in affairs of state; each time he submitted a sealed memorial, he would destroy the draft, so that neither his contemporaries nor his own sons and younger relatives could know what he had written.

sentences.zh: 論者或譏群居位拱默；

translations.literal: Some critics mocked Qun for holding office in silent deference;
translations.idiomatic: Some critics mocked Qun for holding office in silent deference;

sentences.zh: 正始中，詔撰群臣上書以為《名臣奏議》，朝士乃見群諫事，皆歎息焉。

translations.literal: in the Zhengshi era, an edict ordered that memorials submitted by the ministers be compiled into the Memorials of Eminent Ministers, and only then did court officials see Qun's remonstrances and all sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengshi era, an edict ordered that memorials submitted by the ministers be compiled into the Memorials of Eminent Ministers, and only then did court officials see Qun's remonstrances and all sigh in admiration.

sentences.zh: 袁子論曰：或云：「少府楊阜豈非忠臣哉！

translations.literal: Yuan Hong remarked: Some say, "Was not the Privy Treasurer Yang Fu a loyal minister!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong remarked: Some say, "Was not the Privy Treasurer Yang Fu a loyal minister!"

sentences.zh: 見人主之非則勃然觸之，與人言未嘗不道。

translations.literal: When he saw that the ruler was in error, he would flare up and confront him; in speaking with others he never failed to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw that the ruler was in error, he would flare up and confront him; in speaking with others he never failed to speak of it.
